{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mn-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"7dce23b65d7384dcb50ce2ffafadde36599bfd376cc78951b79ece4bf9816cb5","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mn-class-d:lineage:46","source_registry_sha256":"960e2daa314aff60b32f5124e42324d79615ce2a3ea953a336216b4593c0c910","source_liveness_sha256":"0b70283fc58b1f8ea1822994a92e3ce7ff4b722004376a9cd819180969b6fe1e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driving conditions part one confusables and continuation facts","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: SIPDE scanning targets, stopping distance factors, headlight rules, freeway basics, interchanges, exits, crash steps, distractions, aggressive driving and trailer loading","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: SIPDE scanning targets, stopping distance factors, headlight rules, freeway basics, interchanges, exits, crash steps, distractions, aggressive driving and trailer loading
Confusable pairs from the first half of the driving conditions chapter, followed by continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A01
The only eyes you can truly rely on are your own, since nothing you do guarantees that other drivers will see you. [A01]
Why it matters: group SIPDE; prereq for the scanning step.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A01
While scanning, look for oncoming traffic that may turn in front of you, traffic from the left and right including bicycles and pedestrians, traffic coming up behind, and hazardous road conditions. [A01]
Why it matters: group SIPDE scan; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A01
In the Decide step you work out in advance what you would do if the situation changed quickly, and you keep making such decisions as traffic changes. [A01]
Why it matters: group SIPDE; confusable predict versus decide; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A02
Good reference points for the three-second count include a telephone pole, signpost, tree or bridge, and if you are too close, slow gradually until the gap is safe. [A02]
Why it matters: group following distance; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A02
Stopping distance also grows with the time it takes you to see and recognize the danger, before the reaction time to the brake even begins. [A02]
Why it matters: group stopping distance; confusable recognition time versus reaction time.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A02
Before a night drive, study maps and directions, check that your lights work, and make sure the windshield is clean and free of defects. [A02]
Why it matters: group night driving; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A02
Headlights go on at sunset and stay on until sunrise, and are also needed in rain, snow, hail, sleet or fog or whenever you cannot clearly see 500 feet of road ahead. [A02]
Why it matters: group headlights; confusable visibility trigger versus high beam reach; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A02
Low beam is required at two different distances: 1,000 feet for an oncoming vehicle, but only 200 feet when you are following one. [A02]
Why it matters: group headlights; confusable oncoming versus following distance; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A03
Freeways are multi-lane, divided highways with limited access and no stops or cross traffic, so you can travel long distances without stopping. [A03]
Why it matters: group freeways; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A03
Ramp meters are used in metropolitan areas to reduce jams and crashes and to ease merging, and only one car may go on each green. [A03]
Why it matters: group ramp meters; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A03
To change lanes to pass or to leave the freeway, signal and make sure your path is clear before moving over. [A03]
Why it matters: group freeway lanes; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A04
A bus using the shoulder gives way to any traffic merging, entering or exiting, and to other vehicles already on the shoulder. [A04]
Why it matters: group bus shoulders; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A04
An interchange links a freeway to a road or to another freeway through a set of ramps, so you can change roads without disrupting traffic, and the cloverleaf is one of the designs shown. [A04]
Why it matters: group interchanges; the designs themselves are drawings only.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A05
Diverging diamonds give drivers a longer sight distance at turns and make wrong-way entry to ramps extremely difficult. [A05]
Why it matters: group diverging diamond; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A05
At a diverging diamond, pedestrians cross to the middle of the bridge and walk between the traffic lanes with protective barriers on both sides. [A05]
Why it matters: group diverging diamond; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A05
For a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights on the shoulder, move a lane away if you safely can and otherwise slow down; for one coming up behind with a siren, pull to the nearest side and stop. [A05]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; confusable stopped versus approaching; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A06
Learn where your exit is before you start, watch the exit signs, then signal and move into the deceleration lane to slow down without blocking faster traffic. [A06]
Why it matters: group exits; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec11-R18 | anchor: A06
After a crash, exchange driver's license and insurance information with the other drivers, write down their plate numbers, and consider swapping vehicle identification numbers too. [A06]
Why it matters: group crashes; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec11-R19 | anchor: A06
Distracted drivers miss hazards and react more slowly, which shrinks their margin of safety. [A06]
Why it matters: group distraction; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec11-R20 | anchor: A06
Distractions inside the vehicle include using a phone or GPS, reaching for items, eating and drinking, adjusting the radio, talking to passengers and reading, and even looking at a crash scene or daydreaming pulls attention away. [A06]
Why it matters: group distraction; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec11-R21 | anchor: A07
Aggressive driving usually means driving faster than nearby traffic, which leads to tailgating, abrupt lane changes often without signaling, passing on the shoulder, and glaring at or threatening others. [A07]
Why it matters: group aggressive driving; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec11-R22 | anchor: A07
Aggressive drivers tend to have little concern for others and show anger and frustration rooted in their own mindset rather than in other drivers' actions. [A07]
Why it matters: group aggressive driving; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec11-R23 | anchor: A07
A loaded trailer should carry 10 to 15 percent of its weight on the hitch and sit with its floor level. [A07]
Why it matters: group trailers; difficulty high.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec11-R24 | anchor: A07
After the first few miles with a trailer, stop and check the hitch, tires, lights and load, and repeat the check at every rest stop. [A07]
Why it matters: group trailers; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec11-R25 | anchor: A07
Drive slower with a trailer because its smaller wheels spin faster and can overheat the wheel bearings, and because your car brakes were probably not built for heavy trailer loads, so a hard stop at high speed could overturn both vehicles. [A07]
Why it matters: group trailers; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec11-R26 | anchor: A07
Load limits differ by direction: three feet ahead of the front, a flag once the overhang behind reaches four feet, none past the left fender line, and up to six inches past the right fender line. [A07]
Why it matters: group loads; confusable front, rear and side limits; difficulty high.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0082]
